item.title: First social media came after teens. Now AI is doing the same thing
item.description: A major lawsuit against Meta hit the same week OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Teens. Why do stronger protections so often arrive only after mass adoption? Two major things that may at first seem unconnected are happening in tech this week. In a California court, 29 attorneys general are bringing a lawsuit against Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, alleging the company knowingly designed Facebook and Instagram to addict children, misled the public about the harms its platforms posed to young users, and illegally collected data from children under 13 without parental con...

item.title: What to do when there’s too much information, and you don’t know who to trust
item.description: We’re no longer short on information. Today, our problem is an abundance of information and an inability to distinguish fact from fiction. Information overload is causing a credibility crisis. True, it’s never been easier to access the right answers to our questions. But at the same time, that answer is harder to find. There are so many experts, politicians, celebrities, and influencers who are entering their opinions into the chat, and separating good information from bad now feels like finding a needle in a haystack....

item.title: This cheerful Brooklyn playscape is intergenerational by design
item.description: A little bit playground, a little bit park, this playscape at Marlboro Houses in Brooklyn uses abstraction to invite open-ended play and social interaction among the residents. There’s really no wrong or right way to use the new playscape at Marlboro Houses, a New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) campus in the Gravesend neighborhood of Brooklyn. The abstract, bright-yellow play structures are composed of undulating forms that can serve as benches, slides, hills to climb atop, nooks to hide inside, and portals to gaze through. Each of the forms is open to interpretation, inviting curiosity....
